svg.aria-label: How to write ഏ ഴ: 2 letters, ഏ, ഴ, one after another
svg.title: Writing ഏ ഴ
svg.desc: 2 letters written one after another: ഏ, ഴ (malayalam). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansMalayalam-Static.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: ഏ: Rodney F. Moag, Malayalam: A University Course and Reference Grammar (University of Texas at Austin South Asia Institute and COERLL, updated April 2018; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Table II 'How to Write Word-Initial Vowel Symbols', p. xviii: movements 1-7 for ഏ, written by hand by Thomas Joseph <https://github.com/matjic/malayalam/blob/7141acd2f310bc8928822a7aec61d1149efa6fa3/docs/assets/images/front-writing-028.jpg>; ഴ: Sriveenkat, Ml ഴ order.gif, Malayalam letter LLLA stroke-order animation, 00:03.0–00:07.4 (Wikimedia Commons, 1 July 2023) <https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ml_%E0%B4%B4_order.gif>. Source notes on variation: ഏ: Moag's Table II (p. xviii) starts at the foot of the small left arch and climbs clockwise over it to the bar (1), draws the bar to the right (2), climbs the stem (3), runs back down it (4), climbs clockwise over the big arch (5), comes down its right side to the middle (6) and rounds the lower bowl to finish at the bottom right (7). Moag's book is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so only these facts (order, start, direction and end) are cited; no drawing is copied. The page is read from the scan in Mathew Jacob's digital edition (github.com/matjic/malayalam, commit 7141acd), which notes that the numbers mark drawing movements that can belong to one continuous stroke, not pen lifts. The grahyam online-handwriting samples (github.com/bluebottlewize/grahyam, no licence, cited as counts only) keep no pen-up marker, but none of the 6 unique samples jumps between consecutive points the way a lift would; they most often start at the middle left (4 of 6) and end at the middle right (3 of 6). SPACE Kerala's Thooval (GPL-3.0, facts only) starts its EE.png at the lower left and ends it at the lower right. Its shape, start and end match Moag's ഏ, which settles that Thooval's EE.png is this letter. Only six grahyam samples exist, so the lift count rests on few recordings: confidence is medium. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Malayalam outline rather than to Moag's drawing; in that outline the stem runs on below the line and round into the big arch, so the run back down the stem follows it there. ഴ: The 47-frame Gayathri-font animation writes ഴ in one uninterrupted run: left entry arch, clockwise right loop, then the descending inner return and lower hook. This is one attested pedagogical order fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Malayalam outline.
svg.text: How it is written — 2 letters, one after another
Letter 1 of 2 — one unbroken stroke · 7 movements
Letter 2 of 2 — one unbroken stroke · 3 movements
Letter 1: stroke order after Rodney F. Moag, Malayalam: A University Course and Reference Grammar (University of Texas at Austin South Asia Institute and COERLL, updated April 2018;
CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Table II 'How to Write Word-Initial Vowel Symbols', p. xviii: movements 1-7 for ഏ, written by hand by Thomas Joseph
Letter 2: stroke order after Sriveenkat, Ml ഴ order.gif, Malayalam letter LLLA stroke-order animation, 00:03.0–00:07.4 (Wikimedia Commons, 1 July 2023)
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
